meta.title: Lba Rda And Council Formal Meeting

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer the item to a new public hearing on June 4, 2024 (LBA Budget for Fiscal Year 2024-25)
votes.description: The LBA Board closed the first public hearing on the Local Building Authority's Capital Projects Fund budget for FY2024-25 and referred it to a second public hearing on June 4, 2024. The budget covers bond debt service for the Glendale and Marmalade Libraries.

votes.motion: Adjourn as the LBA Board and reconvene as the RDA Board
votes.description: Procedural motion to close the Local Building Authority meeting and transition to the Redevelopment Agency Board meeting.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer the item to a new public hearing on June 4, 2024 (RDA Budget for Fiscal Year 2024-25)
votes.description: The RDA Board closed the first public hearing on the Redevelopment Agency's FY2024-25 budget and referred it to a second public hearing on June 4, 2024.

votes.motion: Adjourn as the RDA Board and reconvene as the City Council
votes.description: Procedural motion to close the Redevelopment Agency Board meeting and transition to the Salt Lake City Council meeting.

votes.motion: Approve minutes (work session minutes of March 5, March 19, and April 2, 2024; formal meeting minutes of March 5, 2024; and retreat minutes of January 23, 2024)
votes.description: The Council approved several sets of prior meeting minutes including work session, formal, and retreat minutes from early 2024.

votes.motion: Adopt Joint Ceremonial Resolution 14 of 2024 celebrating June 2024 as Pride Month
votes.description: The Council adopted a joint ceremonial resolution with Mayor Mendenhall recognizing June 2024 as Pride Month in Salt Lake City, affirming the City's support for the LGBTQ+ community.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer items G1–G7 to a future Consent Agenda for action
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing on seven grant applications (BRIC, Jordan River, UDOT sidewalk, and first responders mental health grants) and referred them to a future consent agenda for final action.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Resolution 16 of 2024 (Fairmont Heights Senior Housing Development at 2257 South 1100 East)
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and adopted a resolution approving the public benefit analysis for the Fairmont Heights Project, authorizing the Administration to negotiate final terms with the Housing Authority of Salt Lake City using $5.6 million in CDBG funds for approximately 110 units of affordable senior housing.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Resolution 15 of 2024 (Metropolitan Water District property tax increase for FY2024-25)
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and approved the proposed property tax increase by the Metropolitan Water District of Salt Lake and Sandy for FY2024-25, supporting water conservation and infrastructure investments.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 36 of 2024 (Library Budget Amendment No. 3 for Fiscal Year 2023-24)
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and adopted an ordinance amending the Library Fund budget for FY2023-24, including required annual true-ups of property tax increments for the Utah Inland Port Authority, Convention Center Hotel, and the Redevelopment Agency.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer items G11–G19 to a new public hearing on June 4, 2024 (FY2024-25 City Budget ordinances)
votes.description: The Council closed the first public hearing on the suite of FY2024-25 budget ordinances (including the Library Fund, tax levy, fee schedule, compensation plans, and MOU appropriations) and referred them to a second public hearing on June 4, 2024.

votes.motion: Continue the public hearing on the Capital City Revitalization Zone to a future date
votes.description: The Council continued the public hearing on the proposed Capital City Revitalization Zone (related to potential redevelopment around the Delta Center) to a future date, allowing additional public input before any action is taken.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 37 of 2024 (Ballpark Station Area Rezone – Creation of the MU-8 Zoning District)
votes.description: The Council adopted an ordinance establishing the new Form Based Mixed Use 8 (MU-8) zoning district, designed for mixed-use buildings of eight stories or less, as part of the Ballpark Station Area Plan implementation.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 38 of 2024 (MU-8 Zone Sign Text Amendments)
votes.description: The Council adopted an ordinance amending Title 21A of the Salt Lake City Code to establish sign regulations for the new Form Based Mixed Use 8 (MU-8) zoning district.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 54 of 2024 (Ballpark Station Area Rezone and Text Amendments)
votes.description: The Council adopted an ordinance rezoning properties within the Ballpark Station Area Plan to various zoning districts including MU-8, aligning with the goals and community vision of the Ballpark Station Area Plan.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 55 of 2024 (Ballpark Station Area Rezone at 1058 and 1064 South West Temple)
votes.description: The Council adopted an ordinance rezoning two parcels at 1058 and 1064 South West Temple to Form Based Urban Neighborhood 2, part of the Ballpark Station Area Plan. Council Member Mano recused himself.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 43 of 2024 (Rezone and Master Plan Amendment at approximately 1791 S and 1815 S State Street and 118 E and 120 E Coatsville Avenue) subject to additional development agreement requirements including 5% affordable units at 80% AMI for 15 years, minimum parking of ½ space per dwelling unit, and 1 space per 1,000 sq ft of commercial space
votes.description: The Council rezoned properties at approximately 1791 and 1815 South State Street and 118 and 120 East Coatsville Avenue from CC and R-1/5000 to R-MU, with conditions in the development agreement including affordability requirements and parking minimums. Council Member Mano recused himself.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 39 of 2024 (Rezone at approximately 536 South 200 West from D-2 to D-1)
votes.description: The Council adopted an ordinance rezoning properties at approximately 536 South 200 West and neighboring Orchard Place addresses from D-2 (Downtown Support District) to D-1 (Central Business District), aligning with a recently approved neighboring rezone.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 44 of 2023 amending the FY2024 final budget (Budget Amendment No. 5) for specified items only (A-1, A-2, A-4, A-6, A-7, A-9, D-1, D-2, D-3, D-4, D-6, D-8, D-9, E-1, and Grant Consent Agenda items G-1 through G-4 in sections 4 and 5)
votes.description: The Council adopted a partial budget amendment for FY2023-24 covering fire hydrant rental costs, police recruitment and retention, cemetery road reconstruction, impact fee refunds, transportation plan updates, mobile clean team funding, and various grant and fund transfers, while holding item A-5 (roundabout/traffic calming) for further discussion.

votes.motion: Further adopt item D-7 (Open Streets 2024 in the Granary District and on Main Street Downtown, $250,288 rescoped from prior year funds) contingent upon the contract including addressing bike infrastructure and encouraging alternative transportation
votes.description: The Council approved an additional budget amendment item funding Open Streets 2024 events in the Granary District ($190,000) and on Main Street Downtown ($60,288), with a condition that the contract address bike infrastructure and promote alternative transportation.

votes.motion: Approve Consent Agenda (items L1–L10, including board appointments and setting public hearing dates)
votes.description: The Council approved the full consent agenda, which included setting public hearing dates for two ordinances and approving board appointments and reappointments to the Library Board, Sister Cities Board, Transportation Advisory Board, Arts Council, Business Advisory Board, and Art Design Board.
